edges.description: Loss of PSMD12 reduces proteasome function and perturbs protein homeostasis.
Expanded PSMD12-related disease can include acne through cutaneous or immune intermediates not otherwise modeled here.
Proteasome dysfunction perturbs growth and organelle-homeostasis pathways.
PSMD12 loss is associated with an interferon-stimulated transcriptional response in patient cells.
Altered developmental growth control and neuronal mitochondrial turnover contribute to delayed milestones.
Neurodevelopmental disruption contributes to persistent cognitive impairment.
Developmental pathway disruption contributes to delayed communication milestones.
Perturbed neurodevelopmental signaling contributes to autism spectrum features.
Dysregulated morphogenesis contributes to craniofacial dysmorphism.
Disturbed developmental programs contribute to skeletal anomalies.
Disturbed developmental programs can specifically include preaxial hand abnormalities.
Congenital malformations in STISS cohorts can involve the heart through uncharacterized developmental intermediates.
Congenital malformations in STISS cohorts can involve the kidneys through uncharacterized developmental intermediates.
Altered developmental growth control contributes to reduced stature.
Later-childhood metabolic dysregulation may contribute to obesity.
Dysregulated type I interferon signaling is associated with interferonopathy-like cutaneous chilblain lesions in a subset of patients.
Elevated expression of type I interferon-stimulated genes in peripheral blood serves as a functional readout of proteasome-stress-induced innate immune signaling in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome.
